files.summary: Window manager spec. Covers: the framework-free compositor as the only writer of geometry and z-index (WM-01); the WinRec registry on dsa/hashtable plus the dsa/zorder list; focus and z renumbering 1..n with a 1,000 ms user-activation rule so background processes cannot steal focus (WM-02); pointer-capture drag and 8-handle resize with the rAF flush in TypeScript pseudocode, a 4 px drag threshold and a frozen content box during live resize (WM-03); clamp rule, 8 px snap zones and a 12 px edge magnet; min/max/restore/full-screen animated with WAAPI FLIP on transform and opacity only, zero under reduced motion; title-bar double-click. Keyboard bindings were checked against Chrome's documented shortcuts and GNOME's Alt+Above_Tab default: Alt+` with Alt+J/K as alternates for switching, the window menu moved off Alt+Space to Alt+W, and an Alt+Left/Right navigation guard. Also: taskbar grouping by app with count and activity badges; tray with exact OFF-04/OFF-05 strings; close = SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after 3 s, with an optional close guard; minimised eviction class, dehydrate-before-page-out protocol and a Restoring overlay with real byte progress (WM-05); display-channel and view-port allow-list (including tty.ack); session layout schema, save and restore (WM-06); secure prompt in a closed shadow root on the secure layer, used for the su password and the agent tty-confirm strip; notifications; a frame meter with vsync-quantised intervals plus LoAF counts; the WCAG table; the extended compositor-port message types; the 10-window Chrome-trace test method (PipelineReporter frames, median of 3 runs); tests for every WM ID. All 5 Mermaid diagrams render with mermaid-cli.

UI design system spec. The full normative tokens.css: colour roles in light-dark(), terminal ANSI 0-15, syntax colours, system font stacks and type scale, 4-pt spacing, radii, sizes, elevation, motion with reduced-motion zeros and a Settings override, z-layers, forced-colours block. Loaded in Chrome 153: it resolves in both themes and compresses to about 2.3 KB gzip. Research-draft --pl-border and light --pl-success were adjusted because the draft values compute below their own 3:1 and 4.5:1 rules. Includes a computed WCAG contrast table (all pairs pass); a restrained 'dense metal, one orbit' identity with no hazard or weapons imagery; the probe-element method for resolving tokens in JS (verified: getPropertyValue returns light-dark() unresolved); component rules; a screen-flow state diagram; screen specs with layout, exact strings, states, a11y, owner and gate for the boot splash, boot menu, verbose log, kernel panic, recovery console, login (offline and guest), desktop, taskbar, launcher and switcher, window chrome and overlays, secure prompt and kernel-confirmation strip, Terminal (xterm 6 options confirmed in its typings, incl. minimumContrastRatio 4.5), File Explorer with semantic search citations and RAG notices, Text Editor banners (conflict, lock, quota), Task Manager (Processes, Memory, Predictions, Services, Performance), Settings (About, Appearance, Memory, Scheduler, Privacy, Boot, Keyboard, Accessibility, Accounts, Developer), agent confirmation block, notifications. Also a WCAG 2.2 AA rule table, the axe matrix in both themes, tokens.json export and a DSN test list.

Shell and terminal spec. Architecture: xterm = TTY device, kernel/core/tty line discipline, term process, sh process, complete service. TTY modes, control characters, signals table (Linux numbering), flow control with at most one 64 KiB output batch per frame, a 256 KiB queue and view acks; SIGTTIN, SIGWINCH, SIGHUP. Shell start-up, prompt and environment ($HOME $PATH $USER etc.). Lexer and ISO EBNF grammar (words, single/double quotes, escapes, $VAR/${VAR}, |, >, >>, <, n>&m, ;, &&, ||, &, ! negation), plus an explicit table of unsupported constructs, each of which runs nothing on the line. Expansion order, builtins vs programs (subshell rule via sh -c), PATH lookup, pipelines, redirections, exit codes, job control with a state diagram, line editor, persisted history (~/.sh_history 0600, history -c clears the hist trie). Tab completion via the complete service with trie namespaces cmd, path (dir-inode keyed so moving a directory is incremental), flag and hist; the kernel checks permissions on the queried directory. Also: incremental VFS updates, a degraded fallback, the complete --bench method; kernel TTY takeover rules for agent confirmation; man pages at apps/bin/man/*.md with JSON front matter as the single source of flags; exact errno texts and output conventions including name escaping. The command reference gives synopsis, flags, output, syscalls, errors, owner and an example for every §9.6 command plus svcctl, debug, swapctl and complete --bench, and an extras table. A 30-step SYS-02 scripted session, interface types, a syscall usage table, performance budgets and tests per SYS/SHL ID and per command. Both Mermaid diagrams render.

cross_spec_requests: 01-architecture/architecture.md + syscall-abi.md: adopt the compositor-port extensions in window-manager.md §4.3. New fields on create: app, activation, limits, ports. New messages: suspend, attach, restoreFailed, notResponding, closeGuard, secure.open/error/close, notify, events. Back-channel: dehydrated, kill, launch, power, layout, secure.result, viewCrashed, ready. Also the display-channel schema (§4.4), the view-port allow-list (window.setTitle, window.requestFocus, window.close, tty.input, tty.winsize, tty.ack, ai.search.focus; everything else EPERM) and a new window.setCloseGuard syscall.

syscall-abi.md: add the calls marked 'requested' in shell-and-terminal.md §4.8: chdir, copy (bulk cp -r), proc.list, tcgetattr, tcsetattr, tcgetpgrp, tty.open, tty.hangup, tty.input, tty.winsize, tty.ack, quota.get, fsck.server, svc.control, swap.stat, swap.ctl, swap.bench, debug.delay, debug.status, debug.clear, ai.log, ai.undo, ai.status and complete.*. Also add spawn options (session, ctty, nice, fg), wait options {pgid, any, nohang, untraced} with exitReason in the result, a 'tty' fd type in fstat, and event topics tty.output and proc.cwd. Add config.get/config.set for device settings (guest -> EACCES, out of range -> EINVAL, audited). Confirm there is no EINTR: interrupted blocking calls return ECANCELED.

03-kernel/processes-and-scheduling.md: define the 12 signals with Linux numbers and default actions (SIGHUP 1, SIGINT 2, SIGKILL 9, SIGPIPE 13, SIGTERM 15, SIGCHLD 17, SIGCONT 18, SIGSTOP 19, SIGTSTP 20, SIGTTIN 21, SIGTTOU 22, SIGWINCH 28). Also define: sessions, process groups and controlling TTYs; SIGTTIN/SIGTTOU rules; SIGHUP on TTY hang-up; SIGTERM then SIGKILL after 3 s for windowed processes; the 1,000 ms user-activation window; notResponding after 5 s of unconsumed display input; the interactive-hint pause (at most 1 s in any 2 s); a suspended process closed without page-in; PRI = priority + nice plus EPRI with aging for ps; the waitingOn values tty:input, tty:output, tty:confirm; the default user-process priority that nice adjusts; runtime changes to sched.quantumMs and sched.tAgeMs, with the recomputed PROC-04 bound published for Settings.

03-kernel/memory-and-paging.md: the 'minimised' eviction class covers the owning pid and its TTY session. Page-out of a windowed process waits for compositor 'dehydrated {wid, lastSeq}' (250 ms timeout) and drains the inbox up to lastSeq before the checkpoint. Restoring progress at most once per frame. Define the proc sub-record of LayoutWindow {osSessionId, pid, pageIds}, the mem.pressure payload, and per-process resident, swapped local/remote, faults, hit ratio, bytes in/out and speculative bytes. Accept runtime mm.budgetMB, mm.softLimitMB and mm.swapTier ('remote' = keep pages only on the server once acked).

02-boot/boot-and-services.md: the session-service restore sequence (create windows in ascending saved z; safe mode restores frames only; an invalid layout is kept as recovery:<id>); router sw event value 'ready' when the precache is installed (drives the Offline-ready badge); router {t:'theme'} at kernel init; svc.* payload {name, state, reason, attempts, nextRetryAt, blockedBy}; handling of {t:'power'}; test-only boot flags (hold splash, open menu, inject cycle, fail storage) for the axe matrix; reboot --menu/--verbose flags; the complete manifest runs the completion service; svcctl require must not validate cycles; the recovery console's two-step confirmation and outbox export.

04-vfs/virtual-file-system.md + 09-database/database.md: add fixed well-known UUIDs (C5 extension) for /usr, /usr/share, /usr/share/man, /usr/share/man/1 and /usr/share/man/2. Seed man pages and index.json read-only there (coherence gap SYS). Define the two-phase, single-transaction copy bulk operation used by cp; whether fd content writes commit per write or at close; and the deterministic tree checksum used by fsck --checksum.

06-sync/offline-and-sync.md: define the net.state payload {state, ops|queued, retryAt} used by the tray; a coalesced last-writer-wins session.layout op (latest per osSessionId in the outbox); and SYNC_WAIT_MS (architecture proposes 10 s), after which bulk commands print 'server confirmation pending'.

08-dsa/data-structures.md: add dsa/zorder (insertTop, insertBelowTop, raise, remove, renumber, bottom-to-top iteration). Keep dsa/hashtable generic over key type (the window registry and PidTable share it). Give dsa/trie removePrefix(prefix) and per-key meta, with bytes/entry reported at 10^3, 10^4 and 10^5, and state in DSA.md why a struct-of-arrays radix trie is used instead of the one-character-per-edge trie. Also: optional dsa/interval (WMD-24), and dsa/ringbuffer for the frame meter.

10-ai/agentic-shell.md: adopt the TTY takeover rules (controlling TTY required else ENOTTY; SIGTTIN for background agents; discard pending input; single key; pastes ignored; default N; 120 s) and the confirmation block layout with name escaping. Send secure.open {kind:'tty-confirm'} and secure.close around each confirmation, use the ai exit codes and messages, and define ai.log, ai.undo and ai.status.

10-ai/rag-semantic-search.md: confirm the Files search UI contract (Name/Content mode switch, ai.search.focus on focus, notices rendered verbatim); semsearch is registered with its man page at apps/bin/man/semsearch.md.

10-ai/predictive-prefetch.md: use compositor 'ready {wid, launchToPaintMs}' as the PRE-03 launch-latency end point and focused/closeRequested as telemetry sources. Provide predict output fields (confidence, reason, model state, prefetch status, --latency data) and ai.telemetry.read/clear/export/setSync for Settings > Privacy.

12-security/security-model.md: record the secure-prompt threat model (same-realm first-party views, closed shadow root, capture-phase key isolation, stacking guarantee, no password in logs or audit, residual risk of pre-hooked DOM APIs), the residual risk that cat of a crafted file can change the terminal title and colours, the SHL-13 name-escaping rule, su audit events, and the no-user-enumeration login rule.

13-quality/testing-and-performance.md: implement the §8.2 drag-trace harness in window-manager.md (trace categories, PipelineReporter frame parser with a golden-trace test, LoAF origin filter, median of 3 runs, nightly and release on the lab-spec runner only). Add the budgets from all three specs to budgets.json, the axe matrix (both themes, forced opposite data-theme, reduced motion, forced colours), the SYS-02 scripted session per release plus its litmus variant, and a traceability check that every command has a 'SYS-02 <command> ...' test.

00-product/identity-and-branding.md: the requested machine-readable token export is wm/tokens/tokens.json (ui-design-system.md §4.1). Clarify that the uname -a p95 <= 5 ms budget is measured from Enter to process exit, since painting waits for the next frame's tty.output batch.
00-product/requirements-traceability.md: register the Plotinium design ID prefixes WMD- (window-manager.md), DSN- (ui-design-system.md) and SHL- (shell-and-terminal.md).
open_questions: Lab OS image (Windows or Ubuntu GNOME)? GNOME binds Alt+` (Above_Tab) by default, and Chrome binds Alt+Space, Alt+Left/Right, Alt+F/E, Alt+Home, Shift+Alt+T, F6 and F10. R3 must run the binding table on the lab image in W5 (the Alt+J/K alternates and Alt+W window menu are the fallback).

Will the instructor accept the Chrome-trace frame metric (PipelineReporter frame durations, median of 3 runs, lab-spec machine) as the WM-03/PROC-05 measurement, with the in-page frame meter as an indicator only?
Lab machine display refresh rate, GPU and screen reader (NVDA or Orca), which affect compositing cost, frame-meter calibration and the manual accessibility pass.
Does the spec's 'full-screen' window state mean a window covering the whole viewport including the taskbar (our reading), or the browser Fullscreen API?

Is a shell without command substitution, subshell groups, here-documents and control-flow keywords an acceptable 'real shell' for SYS-02? Everything §9.6 names is implemented, and unsupported constructs fail with explicit errors.
Is plain-text Terminal scrollback (no colours) after page-in or reboot acceptable, or must the snapshot keep SGR attributes (about 2x memory)?
Will hard links be built? The VFS team decides in W6; ln without -s follows that decision.
Should min/max/restore use WAAPI FLIP (current default) or same-document View Transitions? The W6 spike decides on main-thread cost.
Tagline and team data for Settings > About come from docs/identity/identity.json (the tagline vote is in W2).
